blocks.explanation:
The value of the permutation is given; \(n\) is unknown.
We must find the whole number \(n\).
Plan: write \({}^{n}P_{3}\) as 3 consecutive factors, then write 504 as a product of 3 consecutive numbers.
steps:
Given: \({}^{n}P_{3} = 504\).
To find: \(n\).
Method: \({}^{n}P_{3} = n(n-1)(n-2)\), the product of 3 consecutive whole numbers with largest \(n\). Break 504 into such a product.

Write the permutation as a product
\[{}^{n}P_{3} = \dfrac{n!}{(n-3)!}\]
\[= n(n-1)(n-2)\]
Why: \(n! = n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)!\); the \((n-3)!\) cancels.

Factorise 504
\[504 = 8 \times 63 = 8 \times 9 \times 7\]
\[= 9 \times 8 \times 7\]
Why: 504 is even; \(504 \div 8 = 63 = 9 \times 7\). The three factors 9, 8, 7 are consecutive.

Compare
\[n(n-1)(n-2) = 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7\]
\[n = 9\]
Why: Both sides are products of 3 consecutive whole numbers; the largest factors must match. (For \(n \ge 3\) the product grows with \(n\), so there is only one such \(n\).)

Check
\[{}^{9}P_{3} = 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 = 504 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Substituting \(n = 9\) gives the given value.

blocks.explanation:
The right side is a product of factors counting down from 15.
We must find \(n\).
Plan: count the factors; \({}^{15}P_{n}\) has exactly \(n\) factors.
steps:
Given: \({}^{15}P_{n} = 15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11\) (the dot before 11 is missing in print).
To find: \(n\).
Method: \({}^{15}P_{n} = 15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdots\) with exactly \(n\) factors, the last one being \(15 - n + 1\).

Write \({}^{15}P_{n}\) as a product
\[{}^{15}P_{n} = 15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdots (16 - n)\]
Why: \({}^{n}P_{r} = n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)\); with 15 in place of \(n\) and \(n\) in place of \(r\), the last factor is \(15 - n + 1 = 16 - n\).

Compare the last factor
\[16 - n = 11\]
\[n = 5\]
Why: The given product ends with 11. Equivalently, count the factors 15, 14, 13, 12, 11: there are 5.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints \({}^{15}P_{n} = 15.14.13.12\ 11\), with the multiplication dot between 12 and 11 missing. It should read \({}^{15}P_{n} = 15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11\) (a product of five numbers, not "12 11"). The answer \(n = 5\) is for this corrected form.

blocks.explanation:
A ratio of two permutations is given.
We must find \(n\).
Plan: write the ratio as a fraction, expand both permutations, cancel the common factors, then find 3 numbers that fit.
steps:
Given: \({}^{n}P_{5} : {}^{n-2}P_{2} = 540 : 1\).
To find: \(n\).
Method: A ratio \(a : b = 540 : 1\) means \(\frac{a}{b} = 540\). Expand \({}^{n}P_{5}\) (5 factors from \(n\)) and \({}^{n-2}P_{2}\) (2 factors from \(n-2\)).

Expand both
\[{}^{n}P_{5} = n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n-4)\]
\[{}^{n-2}P_{2} = (n-2)(n-3)\]
Why: 5 factors counting down from \(n\); 2 factors counting down from \(n - 2\).

Cancel the common factors
\[\dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n-4)}{(n-2)(n-3)} = 540\]
\[n(n-1)(n-4) = 540\]
Why: \((n-2)(n-3)\) is on top and bottom. It is not zero because \(n \ge 5\).

Find \(n\)
\[540 = 10 \times 54 = 10 \times 9 \times 6\]
\[n(n-1)(n-4) = 10 \cdot 9 \cdot 6\]
\[n = 10\]
Why: We need three numbers of the form \(n\), \(n - 1\), \(n - 4\). With \(n = 10\) they are 10, 9, 6, and \(10 \times 9 \times 6 = 540\). The left side increases with \(n\) (for \(n \ge 5\)), so no other \(n\) works.
